# Manual testing

<!-- Generated by `pnpm qa:docs` from apps/desktop/src/qa/checklist.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

This is everything automation cannot confirm. It is the same list the app shows in its **QA
checklist** panel (Ctrl+Shift+Q, or Settings > About > QA checklist panel). Use the panel: each
item has a one-click setup, Pass / Fail / Skip, and a button that opens a prefilled GitHub issue.

## How the process works

1. A change that automation cannot fully verify adds its items to `checklist.ts` and lists their
   IDs under **Needs your eyes** in the pull request. `pnpm qa:docs` refreshes this file.
2. You open the panel, work through "Not tested", and answer each item.
3. A failure becomes a GitHub issue (labels `qa-failure`, `needs-triage`, `area:*`) through the
   panel's **Report on GitHub** button; you review it and press Submit on GitHub.
4. A fix references the issue. Items whose question changed get a new `rev`, which clears the old
   answer. **Copy results** puts a Markdown report on the clipboard.

Checklist version 1, 28 items.

## Splash and Home

### SPLASH-01: Splash appears at once and hands off cleanly

Needs the Windows desktop app. Panel setup: `reload-app`.

1. Quit Geeked completely (tray: Quit, or close the window).
2. Start it again from the shortcut.
3. Watch the first second.

**Expected:** The spinning GEEKED logo is on screen almost immediately (no blank white or black flash), stays about a second, then fades into the PIN lock (or Home with no PIN) with no layout jump.

### SPLASH-02: Logo frame rate follows the performance tier

Needs the Windows desktop app. Panel setup: `tier-lightest`.

1. Press "Set up" to switch to the Lightest tier, then reload.
2. Look at the splash logo.
3. Switch to Accelerated and reload again.

**Expected:** Lightest shows one still frame; Accelerated spins noticeably faster and smoother than Balanced.

### HOME-01: Home has a still logo and a different line each launch

Needs the Windows desktop app. Panel setup: `go-home`.

1. Open Home (the house icon).
2. Note the top-left logo and the line under the Geeked mark.
3. Restart the app twice and note the line each time.

**Expected:** The top-left logo never moves; the center mark stays; the line is different on each launch and uses your name or real stats when it can.

## PIN and lock

### LOCK-01: The circles take typing, paste and Backspace

Needs the Windows desktop app. Panel setup: `open-settings-security`.

1. Set a PIN in Settings if none exists, then lock with Ctrl+L.
2. Without clicking anything, type a mix of letters, numbers and symbols.
3. Press Backspace twice, then paste a 6-character PIN with Ctrl+V.
4. Check the Unlock button with fewer than 4 characters typed.

**Expected:** Characters fill the circles as you type; Backspace removes them; paste fills up to 8; no text field is visible; Unlock is disabled under 4 characters and Enter unlocks with the right PIN.

### LOCK-02: Reveal shows characters in the circles and resets

Needs the Windows desktop app.

1. On the lock screen type 4 or more characters.
2. Click the eye button, then click it again.
3. Unlock, lock again with Ctrl+L.

**Expected:** Revealed circles show the real characters in the mono font; hidden shows dots; after locking again the reveal is off.

### LOCK-03: A wrong PIN shakes, clears and slows down

Needs the Windows desktop app.

1. On the lock screen enter a wrong PIN and press Enter, five times.
2. Try the right PIN during the countdown.
3. Wait for the countdown to end and enter the right PIN.

**Expected:** Each wrong PIN shakes and clears the circles; after the fifth a "Locked for 30s" countdown shows and even the right PIN is refused until it ends; then it unlocks.

### LOCK-04: A PIN from an earlier version still unlocks (once)

Needs the Windows desktop app.

1. Only if you set a PIN before the Argon2id change and have not unlocked since.
2. Start Geeked and enter the old PIN.
3. Lock and unlock again.

**Expected:** The old PIN unlocks the first time and keeps working afterwards (it was upgraded in place); nothing asks you to set a new one.

### LOCK-05: Forgot PIN erases everything and restarts setup

Needs the Windows desktop app. **Erases local data.**

1. Make a throwaway chat first (this test erases local data).
2. On the lock screen click "forgot PIN?".
3. Read the warning, type DELETE, press "Erase and reset".

**Expected:** The warning says nothing can be recovered; Erase stays disabled until DELETE is typed; afterwards the app restarts into onboarding with no chats and no PIN.

## Onboarding

### ONB-01: The whole flow works from the keyboard

Needs the Windows desktop app. Panel setup: `restart-onboarding`.

1. Press "Set up" to restart onboarding.
2. Complete every step using only Tab, Enter, Space and arrow keys.

**Expected:** Every control is reachable and visibly focused; Enter continues; the step list responds to arrow keys; you land on Home.

### ONB-02: Name rules are clear

Needs anywhere. Panel setup: `restart-onboarding`.

1. On the name step enter only spaces, then 33 characters, then " Ada ".

**Expected:** Next stays disabled with a clear message for the first two; " Ada " is saved as "Ada" and used in greetings.

### ONB-03: The preview card matches the real app

Needs the Windows desktop app. Panel setup: `restart-onboarding`.

1. On the Performance and appearance step pick a palette, an accent, Compact density and a larger font.
2. Finish onboarding and look at the explorer and text size.

**Expected:** The preview card reflected each change as you made it, and the app looks the same way afterwards.

## Window, tray and startup

### SHELL-01: Resizing from the edges and corners works

Needs the Windows desktop app.

1. Drag each edge and each corner of the window.
2. Try to make it smaller than the minimum.

**Expected:** All eight handles resize; the window stops at 720 by 480.

### SHELL-02: Window buttons and toolbar behave

Needs the Windows desktop app.

1. Use minimize, maximize and close at the top right.
2. Double-click an empty part of the toolbar.
3. Drag the toolbar.

**Expected:** Buttons are in the order minimize, maximize, close; double-click toggles maximize; dragging moves the window.

### SYS-01: Tray icon and menu

Needs the Windows desktop app. Panel setup: `open-settings-system`.

1. Open Settings > System and set "When I close the window" to Minimize to tray.
2. Find the Geeked icon in the system tray.
3. Right-click it and try Open, New chat, Lock, then Quit.

**Expected:** The icon is there; Open shows the window; New chat opens a new thread; Lock shows the PIN screen; Quit exits completely.

### SYS-02: Close to tray hides and locks

Needs the Windows desktop app.

1. With a PIN set and Minimize to tray on, click the window close button.
2. Open Geeked again from the tray icon.

**Expected:** The window hides (the app keeps running in the tray) and, when shown again, asks for the PIN.

### SYS-03: Start with Windows

Needs the Windows desktop app. Panel setup: `open-settings-system`.

1. Turn on "Launch Geeked when Windows starts".
2. Open Task Manager > Startup apps and look for Geeked.
3. Sign out and back in (or restart).
4. Turn the setting off again and check Task Manager.

**Expected:** Geeked appears in Startup apps when on and starts after signing in; it is gone from the list when off.

## Appearance and performance

### APPEAR-01: Theme "System" follows Windows live

Needs the Windows desktop app. Panel setup: `open-settings-appearance`.

1. Set Theme to System in Settings > Appearance.
2. Switch Windows between light and dark mode (Settings > Personalization > Colors).

**Expected:** Geeked switches theme without a restart.

### APPEAR-02: Palette and accent read well everywhere

Needs the Windows desktop app. Panel setup: `open-settings-appearance`.

1. Try each palette and a custom accent in both themes.
2. Visit chat, Settings, the lock screen and a dialog.

**Expected:** Text stays readable and the accent is used consistently; nothing looks washed out.

### APPEAR-03: Animation setting is respected

Needs the Windows desktop app. Panel setup: `open-settings-appearance`.

1. Set Animations to Off, reload, and look at the splash, a wrong PIN and Home.
2. Set it to Reduced and compare.

**Expected:** Off: no shake, no fades and a still logo. Reduced: short fades and a slower logo.

## Providers and keys

### PROV-01: Claude is detected automatically

Needs a real login or API key. Panel setup: `open-settings-agents`.

1. Make sure you are signed in to Claude Code.
2. Open Settings > AI agents.

**Expected:** The Claude card says Connected without any action from you.

### PROV-02: A Grok API key lands in Credential Manager and works

Needs a real login or API key. Panel setup: `open-settings-agents`.

1. In Settings > AI agents paste an xAI API key on the Grok card and save.
2. Open Windows Credential Manager > Windows Credentials and look for a "geeked" entry.
3. Start a chat with Grok.
4. Remove the key in Geeked and check Credential Manager again.

**Expected:** An entry named api-key:xai under the geeked service appears and is gone after Remove; the chat answers; the key never shows in any file or in the database.

### PROV-03: ChatGPT sign-in through the Codex CLI

Needs a real login or API key. Panel setup: `open-settings-agents`.

1. Install the Codex CLI (npm i -g @openai/codex) if needed.
2. On the ChatGPT card click "Sign in with ChatGPT CLI" and finish in the terminal window.
3. Start a chat with ChatGPT.

**Expected:** The card turns Connected within a few seconds and the chat answers.

### PROV-04: Grok CLI sign-in (beta)

Needs a real login or API key. Panel setup: `open-settings-agents`.

1. Install the Grok CLI and run its sign-in from the Grok card.
2. Remove any stored Grok key, then start a Grok chat.

**Expected:** Replies stream as plain text; the card says the CLI route is beta and gives no token counts.

### PROV-05: Provider and model are remembered per chat

Needs a real login or API key.

1. Enable two providers, start a chat on one and pick a model in the chat header.
2. Start another chat on a different provider.
3. Reopen the first chat.

**Expected:** Each chat keeps its own provider and model.

## Status feed

### STATUS-01: Status dots reflect the live feed

Needs a network connection. Panel setup: `open-settings-agents`.

1. Open Settings > AI agents and wait a few seconds.
2. Click a status dot, then "Incident details" if there is one.
3. Click "View status history".

**Expected:** Each provider has a coloured dot matching its real state; the popover shows the summary and when it was checked; links open in your browser.

### STATUS-02: Offline falls back to the cached copy

Needs the Windows desktop app.

1. Let the app load the feed once, then quit it.
2. Turn off your network (airplane mode) and start Geeked.
3. Click a status dot.

**Expected:** Dots still show the last known state and the popover says "Offline: showing the copy from ...".

### STATUS-03: A new-model notice appears, dismisses and offers the model

Needs anywhere. Panel setup: `simulate-new-model`.

1. Press "Set up" to simulate a new Claude model.
2. Dismiss the notice.
3. Open the model picker in the chat header.

**Expected:** One notice appears; it dismisses; the new model is in the Claude model list.

### STATUS-04: A degraded provider turns its dot amber

Needs anywhere. Panel setup: `simulate-claude-degraded`.

1. Press "Set up" to simulate a degraded Claude.
2. Look at the picker dot and click it.

**Expected:** The dot is amber and the popover lists the simulated incident.
